AUTHOR: Beyan
TITLE: Extracting statistically significant behaviour from fish tracking data with and without large dataset cleaning
REGION: Kenting National Park, Taiwan (nuclear power plant intake bay)
DATA: Fish4Knowledge project archive: 12,247 10-min videos from a fixed camera, 3,649,007 trajectories with per-video water temperature
V_EV: Sec 3: 'The camera used in this study was at a depth of 2 m ... the scene is greatly affected by illumination variations'
D2: no train/test split (unsupervised mcRBM clustering of all trajectories)
D_EV: no statement found (unsupervised clustering on whole dataset; no split described)
R_EV: Sec 3: 'The videos were captured from one of four fixed cameras ... We selected the data associated with the damselfish'; single camera/site only
C_EV: Sec 3: '1000 of the 3.6 million fish trajectories were manually examined ... 16,504 detections, of which 16,210 were actually fish, 745 trajectories ... correctly tracked'
E_EV: Sec 5.2: 'an increasing trend was obtained for the mean, median and mode speeds with p-values of 0.0032, 0.0056, and 0.0032'
ARCH: Fish4Knowledge covariance tracker + decision-tree species classifier (prior work); B-spline trajectory features + mean-covariance RBM clustering for outlier removal
METR: manual-verification error rate, outlier/inlier agreement with manual labels (52%/78%), speed statistics, Kruskal-Wallis, Mann-Kendall
NOTE: Eligibility: uses full Fish4Knowledge monitoring archive (deployment info: Kenting, fixed camera 2 m depth, temperature) not the F4K recognition benchmark sets -> treated as monitoring-programme data; verifier should confirm vs. lead's F4K benchmark-only rule. Detection/tracking done by prior F4K system; this paper's ML is mcRBM-based trajectory outlier rejection. C1 coded Y for the outlier rejection threshold (A% of median cluster size, A=1-25 tested), C4 Y for reject mechanism; C5 both = manual FP check and incorrect-trajectory (linking) assessment. E1 behaviour = swimming speed vs water temperature; no independent reference.
